samples.claim: pub(crate) project_by_ids recursively selects children, then returns the complete clone when the field id is selected and either no children were separately selected or include_all_children=true. If any child survives otherwise, it returns a trimmed clone; else None. Thus include_all_children=false plus parent-only selection still retains the whole subtree, while parent plus a selected child can trim it. IDs are tested with slice contains per node, not a bitmap; names and atomic blob/map semantics are not considered in this method.

samples.claim: row_id_sequence holds serialized RowIdSequence bytes inline_row_ids=5, or an empty RowLineageColumn marker column_row_ids=12 referring to a file field -3. Row IDs follow physical row order, including unsorted example [1,42,3]. The comments say current writers keep inline bytes regardless of size. Any column arm requires manifest spilled-lineage flag 2048; otherwise an older reader could see an unset oneof and falsely infer no row IDs. This is a schema contract; current writer behavior still needs source confirmation. Empty marker declaration: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305.

samples.claim: Encoding hot paths hoist invariant branches, preallocate contiguous zero-initialized buffers by default, restrict unsafe set_len to measured hot paths with a SAFETY justification that all bytes are initialized before reading, dispatch spawn_cpu only at the async/CPU boundary without nesting, and use existing next-item helpers. The rule does not prove any specific unsafe block is sound.
samples.evidence:
83 | ## lance-encoding
84 | 
85 | Performance-critical encoding/decoding paths have additional requirements:
86 | 
87 | - Hoist loop-invariant conditionals out of hot loops — branch once outside, then use separate loop bodies or monomorphized variants.
88 | - Pre-allocate single contiguous buffers. Default to `buf.resize(len, 0)` for safe initialization; reserve `Vec::with_capacity` + `unsafe { set_len() }` for measured hot paths only, with a `// SAFETY:` comment explaining why the buffer will be fully initialized before read (e.g., immediately followed by `read_exact`).
89 | - Use `spawn_cpu()` only at the async-to-CPU boundary (e.g., FSST, decompression, batch materialization) — never nest redundant `spawn_cpu()` calls.
90 | - Use `expect_next()` and similar utility methods instead of inlining `None`-checks with error returns.
samples.review_notes: Manually confirmed claim against complete sampled numbered evidence.

samples.claim: null_offset_adjustment uint64=2 must exceed total item length so a null marker does not collide with a valid end offset; the proposed optimal choice is 1+number of items to minimize required bits. num_items uint64=3 counts items referenced by this offsets page, allowing it to map to child item pages. Integer overflow and malformed offsets require implementation validation; none occurs here.

139 |     /* If a list is null then we add this value to the offset
140 |      *
141 |      * This value must be greater than the length of the items so that
142 |      * (offset + null_offset_adjustment) is never used by a non-null list.
143 |      *
144 |      * Note that this value cannot be equal to the length of the items
145 |      * because then a page with a single list would store [ X ] and we
146 |      * couldn't know if that is a null list or a list with X items.
147 |      *
148 |      * Therefore, the best choice for this value is 1 + # of items.
149 |      * Choosing this will maximize the bit packing that we can apply to the offsets.
150 |      */
151 |     uint64 null_offset_adjustment = 2;
152 |     /* How many items are referenced by these offsets.  This is needed in
